# Beyond the GRPO name: advantage scales, clipping units, and train–rollout mismatch

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/policy-optimization.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-09 · 56 topic entries / 8 representative comparisons

The GRPO family differs in how rewards become advantages, which likelihood ratio is clipped, and which distribution produced samples. Dr. GRPO, DAPO, GSPO, and TIS/IcePop modify different parts; not every ratio is the same off-policy correction.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Mechanism comparison {#comparison}

Axes: Advantage scale: group mean, group standard deviation, and length normalization · Update unit: token surrogate or sequence ratio · Sampling validity: zero-variance groups and dynamic resampling · Distribution roles: current training policy, old training policy, and rollout engine

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Identify the numerator and denominator before discussing stability

GSPO aggregates response log-ratios of current versus old policy. TIS and IcePop compare probabilities under the same weights across training and rollout engines. One controls update size and the other corrects implementation mismatch. A training loop can need both; neither automatically covers the other's bias.

Sources: [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md) · [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md) · [IcePop](../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en.md)

### Normalization changes weights, not missing signals

GRPO standard deviation, its removal in Dr. GRPO, and DAPO aggregation over valid tokens alter sample contributions. An all-right or all-wrong group can still have no direction after centering. Dynamic sampling controls whether such groups reach updates. Count discarded generation work, not just optimizer steps.

Sources: [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md) · [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md)

### Choose the update event before clipping: text and decisions are different variables

GRPO/GSPO mainly change advantages or ratio units of an existing text policy. RLiD first changes the probability event to a compiled menu action. Its Rao–Blackwell account conditions on alternative wordings of the same action within one text policy; it does not prove a separately trained LDM stronger. Afterstate menus, memory provenance, label calibration, and interface matching must be specified first. Sharing a PPO formula does not remove these differences.

Sources: [RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs](../../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why does lower variance after text-to-action marginalization not imply RLiD wins every task over reasoning-token policies? {#cross-same-policy-marginalization-not-new-model-win}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The result fixes one text policy and action-dependent advantages, preserving expected updates while removing realization variance. Real LDMs have different parameterizations and training paths, while reasoning adds computation. Temporal credit and menu interfaces remain separate. The paper's Qwen3.5-2B ARC result still favors token policies; that counterexample must be retained.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Two wordings of open from one policy can be marginalized. Replacing it with another label-only network lies outside that same-policy identity.

    Sources: [RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs](../../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en.md) · [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md)

### If all four responses are wrong, does changing GRPO to Dr. GRPO create a learning direction? {#cross-all-failed-group}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not when rewards remain identical: removing standard deviation leaves centered advantages zero. Dr. GRPO changes scale bias; DAPO filters such groups and samples again. If budget never yields distinguishable outcomes, improve exploration or supervision rather than relabel normalization.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: With all rewards zero, subtracting the mean still yields zero. A constant denominator does not make one trajectory better.

    Sources: [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [Dr. GRPO](../../../../post-training/2503.20783-dr-grpo/README-en.md) · [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md)

### Is GSPO equivalent to clipping each token with PPO and then averaging? {#cross-sequence-ratio-not-token-average}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. GSPO aggregates log-ratios into one response ratio before clipping. Per-token clipping applies nonlinear selection first. Averaging and clipping do not commute, so outlier tokens have different effects. Sequence rewards do not mathematically require one unique surrogate.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: With one very high ratio and other ratios near one, per-token clipping can clip just that token; GSPO assigns the aggregate weight to the entire response.

    Sources: [DeepSeekMath / GRPO](../../../../post-training/2402.03300-grpo/README-en.md) · [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md) · [DAPO](../../../../post-training/2503.14476-dapo/README-en.md)

### How do TIS and IcePop handle a very small engine ratio, and is that policy staleness? {#cross-tis-versus-icepop}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** TIS caps only large ratios and retains the small one. IcePop zeros its policy gradient below the lower bound. Both address engine mismatch, not drift between current and old sampling weights. Masking is not standard PPO clipping or a cure for stale policies.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Different kernels giving different probabilities at identical weights is an engine issue. Sampling from weights several updates old introduces separate policy staleness.

    Sources: [TIS](../../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en.md) · [IcePop](../../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en.md) · [GSPO](../../../../post-training/2507.18071-gspo/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-09** · Added RCEA to separate policy optimization from entropy diagnostics. Falling global entropy does not establish that valid strategies contracted. The local component verifies only the trajectory chain rule and first-order local approximation.

Affected: [Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards](../../../../post-training/2611.09448-rcea/README-en.md)

**2026-11-04** · Reviewed RLiD and added the text-event versus executable-action axis. Same-policy variance marginalization is not superiority of differently trained LDMs; label-marginal KL also differs from row entropy. L1 components only; costly full training is not reproduced.

Affected: [RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs](../../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en.md)

**2026-10-27** · Initial edition: compares GRPO/Dr. GRPO/DAPO advantages and normalization, GSPO sequence ratios, and TIS/IcePop engine correction; 54 abstracts reviewed and six papers read closely.
